hypothesis: An alternate modern CDCL solver may decide the preserved full scope-111 DTS CNF within the same bounded budget even though Kissat returned UNKNOWN, producing a validator-accepted witness or a finite-instance UNSAT result.
rationale: The exact one-hot DTS encoding is already generated and hash-preserved. CaDiCaL is a materially different CDCL implementation and provides a bounded solver-portfolio test without changing the frozen mathematical target, encoding, or verifier.
expected_information_gain: SAT yields a true-objective candidate; UNSAT proves only infeasibility of the frozen finite scope-111 decision instance; UNKNOWN from a second solver closes this exact encoding and budget as a solver-portfolio route rather than proving global DTS infeasibility.
method: Run CaDiCaL 2.1.3 with its wall-clock option -t 120 on the existing DIMACS file whose SHA256 is 2f8eeb39da6e114adb765aa9e1f975e558b843ee8320cc6a478eb02b2e1680a3a. Parse any competition-format model, decode the first 3885 one-hot mark variables into seven rows, and independently validate with research_tools/verify_dts.py. Do not regenerate or alter the CNF.
metric: CaDiCaL status, elapsed time, model availability, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: An independently verified decoded model with scope<=111 is exactly true-objective progress. UNSAT is a finite-instance result only; UNKNOWN is runtime evidence.
kill_condition: Stop at SAT, UNSAT, or the 120-second CaDiCaL limit plus bounded process cleanup. Do not infer mathematical infeasibility from UNKNOWN or timeout.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if SAT model passes independent verifier

previous_best_comparison.kissat_full: UNKNOWN under 120-second budget on identical CNF
previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: alternate solver capability on identical full-target encoding

interpretation: CaDiCaL 2.1.3 returned UNKNOWN at the declared 120-second real-time limit on the preserved full scope-111 CNF. No model was emitted, so the target was not reached and no mathematical infeasibility follows.
failure_mode: The alternate full-domain CDCL run also remained unresolved at the declared solver budget; the result is runtime evidence, not an UNSAT certificate.
what_was_learned: Two materially different CDCL solvers, Kissat 4.0.3 and CaDiCaL 2.1.3, both reached UNKNOWN on the same 15540-variable/1461683-clause formula within 120 seconds. The full encoding is therefore not decision-ready at this local budget, despite stable execution and preserved reproducibility.
recommended_next_action: Close the two-solver full-domain SAT portfolio at this encoding and budget. Do not infer global DTS infeasibility; wait for a genuinely different structural decomposition, solver capability, or human-supplied construction.
repetition_justification: This is a bounded alternate-solver comparison on the same frozen CNF, not a repeated Kissat invocation; the solver implementation changes while the mathematical encoding and verification contract remain fixed.
